about: Capture-time provenance for docs/screens/*.png (#335). One row per shot, written by the session that took the pixels: sha256/canvas are properties of the bytes, origin/install/url/seed/level/layout/sampleRate/build are properties of the instrument and cannot be recovered from the PNG afterwards. `node tools/recap.js check` verifies each row against the file it addresses and against every other row of the same (seed, level, sampleRate); the vocabulary, the route verdicts and the audio-draw rule live in tools/recap.js, not here.

4abba57.note: The four blobs that draw a frame, sha256, read from the checkout that ran the capture. index.html plus the three js/ files that put a pixel on screen: js/10_assets.js makes the textures, js/20_level.js the lit materials, js/40_render.js is the rasterizer. `node tools/recap.js check` recomputes them from the tree it runs in and prints whether these frames still show what that tree ships (#536). The session that took these pixels proved this build off the wire, blob by blob, against the deployed page.

39edaf3.note: The twelve blobs that build serves - index.html and every script its own index.html loads - as sha256, read from that build. `node tools/recap.js check` recomputes them from the tree it runs in and prints whether these frames still show what that tree ships (#536). This entry is a BIND RE-KEY, not a capture: the pixels were taken at b7a40d6 by the pass described in tools/recap.js and README.md, and #910 measured what main at 39edaf3 draws from the same route - all eight poses re-rendered off https://lioreshai.github.io/breach-protocol-flash-next/ after that deploy sha256-matched origin/main four for four. The frames came back with no world pixel moved: three of the eight are byte-identical to the committed bytes and the other five differ only inside the columns the held rig occupies (0.03% to 0.39% of the frame, every mean within 0.01 luma), which is the load-to-load disagreement #611 already names, not a surface being fetched differently. So the PNGs are carried and only the bind moves. The blob that moved is js/20_level.js, and what moved in it is a jump predicate (#893): a still frame cannot show it because the feet are on the ground.

7f74a90.note: The twelve blobs that build serves - index.html and every script its own index.html loads - as sha256, read from that build, and proved off the wire before the record moved to it: for each of them the bytes served by https://lioreshai.github.io/breach-protocol-flash-next/ sha256-match `git show 7f74a90:<file>`, 12 for 12. `node tools/recap.js check` recomputes them from the tree it runs in and prints whether these frames still show what that tree ships (#536, #925). This entry is a BIND RE-KEY, not a capture: the pixels in the rows that name it were taken at build d7a0196 by the pass tools/livecap.js FRAMES describes, and #924 moved one of the twelve - js/13_mesh.js, whose body-surface gate (#922) now runs out to its own crossover at a projected period of 49.7 px. That is a nearer body than any frame in this set carries, so the eight poses were re-run off that deploy to ask the pixels instead of the hash: two of them (both ABATOIR CORE poses) came back BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed bytes, and the other six differ from them by between 0.00% and 0.28% of the frame with every differing pixel inside the columns the held rig occupies - the load-to-load disagreement #611 already names, not a surface being fetched differently. The three layout signatures came back the same (4083630493 / 2343219222 / 3610925125), so the deal fields these rows carry are still true of the picture they address. The PNGs are therefore carried and only the bind moves, which is the shape #910 recorded for 39edaf3.

shots.note: Re-taken off the deployed page for #931. The bind aged: the frames it replaced were taken at build 7f74a90 and five of the twelve blobs that page serves have moved since (js/00_core.js, js/13_mesh.js, js/20_level.js, js/40_render.js, js/90_dev.js - #922 shipped a body ramp in 13_mesh, #517/#918 the deck-edge row and its crease in 40_render), and the arbiter came back FRAME-MOVED, so a re-take was owed rather than a re-key. The deploy was proved blob by blob first: index.html and every script it loads, 12 in all, sha256-match git show ce6b539:<file> 12 for 12, and the shutter ran on that page afterwards, so these are the pixels the shipped bytes draw and not a harness render. Route: one page load and one boot per pose (js/90_dev.js refuses a second DEV.boot() in a load), the camera on the seat the same deal puts it on, DEV.freeze(true), DEV.set("grain",0), DEV.clear() before the shutter, the display pinned to 1440x763 by livecap's --vp, toDataURL handed back RGBA and the frame re-encoded to colour type 2 through tools/png_rgb.js. The dealt signature is the one the replaced row named, so the dice held and only the paint moved. The audio term is carried rather than read: these headless loads have no output device, so SND.init never sets SND.ac and sampleRate is not readable off the page (#404); the control is that that term sets how many draws precede generation, so had it moved the signature would have moved with it, and it did not.
